_about: Hand-kept market fundamentals for each property type, shown on the real estate overview. No free feed publishes cap rates, vacancy or rent growth by property type, so these are rounded ranges compiled from the public summaries of the reports named in 'sources'. Update 'asOf', 'checked' and the figures after each new round of quarterly reports (cap rate surveys come out twice a year). Live figures (REIT returns, construction spending, building permits, lending rates) come from build_re_invest.py instead.
sources: CBRE research (cap rate surveys, US and Canada market figures)

classes.name: Single-family homes
classes.what: Houses bought to live in or rent out. The biggest asset class by far; prices and rents for every market are live on this page.
classes.drivers: Mortgage rates, local supply and wage growth. Lock-in from low-rate mortgages keeps US resale supply tight.

classes.name: Multifamily (apartments)
classes.what: Rental apartment buildings. A favourite of institutional investors because rent rolls reset every year.
classes.drivers: A record wave of new US supply is being absorbed, so rent growth is weak in the Sun Belt but firmer in the Midwest and Northeast.

classes.name: Office
classes.what: Office towers and suburban office parks. Hit hardest by hybrid work; values are well below their 2019–2022 peaks.
classes.drivers: A split market: the newest, best-located towers are filling up while older buildings face conversion or sale at deep discounts.

classes.name: Industrial and logistics
classes.what: Warehouses, distribution and fulfilment centres, light manufacturing and cold storage.
classes.drivers: E-commerce and near-shoring (Mexico's border markets especially) keep demand up, but a 2022–24 building boom pushed vacancy back toward normal.

classes.name: Retail
classes.what: Shopping centres, strip malls, high streets and single-tenant stores.
classes.drivers: Almost no new shopping centres were built for a decade, so grocery-anchored centres are full and investors have come back.

classes.name: Data centers
classes.what: Buildings that house servers, power and cooling for cloud and AI computing. The fastest-growing property type.
classes.drivers: AI demand means most new space is leased before it is built; power supply, not demand, is the main limit.

classes.name: Hotels
classes.what: Hotels and resorts. Income resets nightly, so it moves with the economy and travel demand.
classes.drivers: Leisure travel has levelled off after the post-pandemic boom; group and international travel are filling the gap.

classes.name: Healthcare and senior housing
classes.what: Senior living, medical offices, hospitals and life-science labs.
classes.drivers: The baby boomers are turning 80 while very little new senior housing is being built.

classes.name: Self-storage
classes.what: Storage units rented by the month. Demand follows moving, downsizing and home sales.
classes.drivers: Slow home sales mean fewer people moving; new supply has slowed, which should help rents recover.

classes.name: Towers and infrastructure
classes.what: Cell towers, fibre and other long-lease infrastructure owned through REITs.
classes.drivers: Behaves more like a bond: very sensitive to long-term interest rates.

classes.name: Net lease
classes.what: Single-tenant buildings (pharmacies, restaurants, distribution) leased for 10–25 years with the tenant paying costs.
classes.drivers: Valued like a bond: the spread over the 10-year government yield decides prices.
